extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting datasets/benchmarks to NeurIPS 2022 D&B track and the track's reviewers
extracted.subtask_short: NeurIPS 2022 Datasets & Benchmarks call for papers
extracted.subtask_description: The NeurIPS 2022 Datasets & Benchmarks track call for papers sets out the track's review criteria and submission requirements, including accessibility and licensing of data, required supplementary materials (datasheets, dataset nutrition labels, accountability frameworks), reproducibility expectations for benchmarks, and the four explicit factors reviewers consider when evaluating submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equally stringent review tailored to datasets/benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: We are aiming for an equally stringent review as the main conference, yet better suited to datasets and benchmarks. Submissions to this track will be reviewed according to a set of criteria and best practices specifically designed for datasets and benchmarks, as described below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The D&B track holds the same stringency bar as the main conference but uses dataset- and benchmark-specific review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility is a key criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A key criterion is accessibility: datasets should be available and accessible, i.e. the data can be found and obtained without a personal request to the PI, and any required code should be open source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessibility is explicitly singled out as a key criterion: data must be findable and obtainable without a personal request to the PI, and supporting code must be open source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required supplementary materials beyond the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Next to a scientific paper, authors should also submit supplementary materials such as detail on how the data was collected and organized, what kind of information it contains, how it should be used ethically and responsibly, as well as how it will be made available and maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary materials must cover collection/organization, contents, ethical/responsible use guidance, and availability/maintenance plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility and quality of the submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility and quality of the submission: Impact, originality, novelty, relevance to the NeurIPS community will all be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First explicit review factor: impact, originality, novelty, and relevance to the NeurIPS community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of relevant documentation (datasets vs. benchmarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Completeness of the relevant documentation: For datasets, sufficient detail must be provided on how the data was collected and organized, what kind of information it contains, how it should be used ethically and responsibly, as well as how it will be made available and maintained. For benchmarks, best practices on reproducibility should be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second explicit review factor: datasets must document collection, organization, contents, ethics, and availability; benchmarks must follow reproducibility best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility and accountability: For datasets, there should be a convincing hosting, licensing, and maintenance plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third explicit review factor: convincing hosting, licensing, and maintenance plans are required for dataset submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and responsible use
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics and responsible use: Any ethical implications should be addressed and guidelines for responsible use should be provided where appropriate. Note that, if your submission includes publicly available datasets (e.g. as part of a larger benchmark), you should also check these datasets for ethical issues. You remain responsible for the ethical implications of including existing datasets or other data sources in your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fourth explicit review factor: authors must address ethical implications, provide responsible-use guidelines, and audit any included third-party datasets, retaining responsibility for those datasets' ethical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind reviewing as default
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing is in principle single-blind, hence the paper should not be anonymized. In cases where the work can be reviewed equally well anonymously, anonymous submission is also allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-blind reviewing is the default for the track because datasets often require non-anonymous repositories; double-blind submission is allowed only when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open review during discussion phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission is single-blind, and the review process is open during the discussion phase. However, only accepted papers will remain visible after the review phase, and the datasets themselves can be released at a later date (see below).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers and reviews are publicly visible during the open discussion phase; only accepted papers remain visible after review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credentialized access only under strict conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: This will be possible on the condition that a credentialization is necessary for the public good (e.g. because of ethically sensitive medical data), and that an established credentialization procedure is in place that is 1) open to a large section of the public, 2) provides rapid response and access to the data, and 3) is guaranteed to be maintained for many years. A good example here is PhysioNet Credentialing, where users must first understand how to handle data with human subjects, yet is open to anyone who has learned and agrees with the rules. This should be seen as an exceptional measure, and NOT as a way to limit access to data for other reasons (e.g. to shield data behind a Data Transfer Agreement). Misuse would be grounds for desk rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open credentialized access is permitted only when (1) necessary for the public good, (2) the credentialing process is broadly accessible, (3) rapid in response, and (4) guaranteed to be long-lived; misuse (e.g., DTA gating) is grounds for desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset documentation frameworks recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission introducing new datasets must include the following in the supplementary materials (as a separate PDF): Dataset documentation and intended uses. Recommended documentation frameworks include datasheets for datasets, dataset nutrition labels, data statements for NLP, and accountability frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New-dataset submissions must include documentation and intended uses, with recommended frameworks: datasheets for datasets, dataset nutrition labels, data statements for NLP, and accountability frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-accessible URL to dataset/benchmark
rubrics_metrics.description: URL to website/platform where the dataset/benchmark can be viewed and downloaded by the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reviewer-accessible URL for viewing/downloading the dataset or benchmark is required in the supplementary materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author statement of responsibility and license confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Author statement that they bear all responsibility in case of violation of rights, etc., and confirmation of the data license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must explicitly assume responsibility for any rights violations and confirm the data license in their supplementary materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting, licensing, and maintenance plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosting, licensing, and maintenance plan. The choice of hosting platform is yours, as long as you ensure access to the data (possibly through a curated interface) and will provide the necessary maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must provide a concrete hosting, licensing, and maintenance plan; the hosting platform is free choice as long as access and maintenance are guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term preservation: It must be clear that the dataset will be available for a long time, either by uploading to a data repository or by explaining how the authors themselves will ensure this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must make long-term availability of the dataset explicit, either via a data repository or a credible author-managed preservation plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit license (CC for data, open source for code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit license: Authors must choose a license, ideally a CC license for datasets, or an open source license for code (e.g. RL environments). An overview of licenses can be found here: https://paperswithcode.com/datasets/license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must explicitly assign a license, ideally a CC license for datasets and an open-source license for accompanying code/RL environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured metadata via web standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Add structured metadata to a dataset's meta-data page using Web standards (like schema.org and DCAT): This allows it to be discovered and organized by anyone. A guide can be found here: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/data-types/dataset. If you use an existing data repository, this is often done automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured machine-readable metadata using schema.org / DCAT is expected so the dataset can be discovered programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent dereferenceable identifier highly recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly recommended: a persistent dereferenceable identifier (e.g. a DOI minted by a data repository or a prefix on identifiers.org) for datasets, or a code repository (e.g. GitHub, GitLab,...) for code. If this is not possible or useful, please explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A persistent dereferenceable identifier (DOI, identifiers.org prefix) is strongly recommended; otherwise a code repo URL, with an explanation if neither is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility framework for benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: For benchmarks, the supplementary materials must ensure that all results are easily reproducible. Where possible, use a reproducibility framework such as the ML reproducibility checklist, or otherwise guarantee that all results can be easily reproduced, i.e. all necessary datasets, code, and evaluation procedures must be accessible and documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark submissions must ensure easy reproducibility, ideally via the ML reproducibility checklist, with accessible and documented datasets/code/evaluation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure for resubmissions retracted from another venue
rubrics_metrics.description: For papers resubmitted after being retracted from another venue: a brief discussion on the main concerns raised by previous reviewers and how you addressed them. You do not need to share the original reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmitted-after-retraction papers must briefly summarize prior reviewer concerns and how they have been addressed, but need not share the original reviews.
